cases.title: Death at the Meridian Observatory
cases.tagline: A director falls from the great telescope on the night of the donor gala. Nobody saw a thing. Everybody is lying about something.
cases.setting: The Meridian Observatory, a privately funded mountain observatory, on the night of its annual donor gala.
cases.briefing: At 23:40 on Saturday night, security guard Nell Okafor found the observatory's director, Dr. Elias Voss (58), dead on the floor of the main dome beneath the telescope gantry. The donor gala had been running in the hall next door since 19:00. Voss was last seen leaving the hall at about 22:25. First responders assumed a fall on the gantry stairs. Three people had reason to quarrel with him that night: his deputy director Dr. Mara Quill, his doctoral student Theo Lark, and board chairman and principal donor Gideon Ashby. The dome corridor camera was not recording. Whether this is an accident or a homicide — and who, if anyone, should answer for it — is for the investigation to establish.

victim.name: Dr. Elias Voss
victim.description: Director of the Meridian Observatory, 58. Brilliant, exacting, and not well liked.

characters.name: Dr. Mara Quill
characters.publicProfile: Deputy director for nine years and administrator of the observatory's research grants. Composed, precise, widely expected to succeed Voss.

characters.name: Theo Lark
characters.publicProfile: Fourth-year PhD student and the telescope's most frequent night operator. Quick-tempered, overworked, argued with Voss in front of the guests.

characters.name: Gideon Ashby
characters.occupation: Chairman of the Board and principal donor
characters.publicProfile: Property magnate, chairman of the observatory's board, and its largest donor. Charming until crossed. Left the gala early.

characters.name: Nell Okafor
characters.publicProfile: Night security at the observatory for six years. Found the body at 23:40 and raised the alarm.

characters.name: Ivo Brandt
characters.publicProfile: Owner of the catering firm hired for the gala. Worked the service corridor behind the hall all evening.

cases.title: The Nightingale Vanishes
cases.tagline: A jewelled clockwork bird sat in a locked vault all week. On appraisal night it turned out to be a fake. Someone switched it — but when?
cases.setting: The Ravel Gallery, a private gallery of decorative arts, during the week of an insurance appraisal.
cases.briefing: On Thursday at 21:40, insurance appraiser Odile Marchetti examined the Ravel Gallery's prize piece — the Nightingale, a nineteenth-century jewelled clockwork bird insured for 3.5 million — in the gallery's vault and declared it a replica. The real bird is gone. The vault was locked all week and nobody reported a break-in. In the previous ten days the bird had been out for restoration and returned on Monday night; the vault was also opened in the small hours of Wednesday. Gallery owner Lucien Ravel recently raised the insurance cover. Restorer Irene Vance had the bird in her studio. Security consultant Felix Dorn built the vault system. Find out when the switch happened, who made it, and whether anyone should be charged.

characters.name: Lucien Ravel
characters.publicProfile: Third-generation gallerist with an old name and, it is whispered, new money troubles. Raised the Nightingale's insurance last month.

characters.name: Irene Vance
characters.publicProfile: Gifted restorer who spent ten days with the Nightingale on her bench and returned it on Monday night. Respected, private, quietly exhausted.

characters.name: Felix Dorn
characters.occupation: Security consultant who installed the vault system
characters.publicProfile: Built the gallery's vault and alarm system two years ago. Knows every code and sensor in the building.

characters.name: Odile Marchetti
characters.publicProfile: Fine-art appraiser for the gallery's insurer. Appraised the Nightingale in 2024 and exposed the fake on Thursday.
